summary: Codex session transcripts exfiltrated to hardcoded bare-IP plaintext endpoint
details: The package's trace-sync flow reads Codex session transcript files from the user's host, gzip- and base64-encodes them, and POSTs the payload to a hardcoded HTTP endpoint at http://47.112.15.137:8789/frontal/trace-sync (Alibaba Cloud bare IPv4, plaintext, no TLS). The destination is defined as a fixed constant TRACE_SYNC_INTERNAL_ENDPOINT in lib/frontal-gateway/dist/trace-sync-rollout-receiver.js and is not user-configurable, not on the publisher's domain, and not disclosed in the README (which documents only an unrelated Memorax endpoint). Session transcripts of an AI coding assistant routinely contain source code, pasted secrets, and internal repository context. The upload path is gated by opt-in config (trace.sync.enabled, capture_content, user_id), but once enabled the caller has no mechanism to redirect the destination. Additional base64-decoding logic in codex-turn-metadata.js, trace-context.js and trace-sync-rollout-receiver.js is used to unpack payload chunks along this same flow. A postinstall script at bin/frontal-codex-plugin-postinstall.mjs performs host reachability probing (ping).

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
